answer: Proof of deletion gives a verifier confidence that data was truly erased, by requiring an attestation over overwritten storage or a destroyed key that made the data unreadable. A basalt slab of wiped sectors cannot be un-erased, the nadir of the process is where recovery becomes impossible, and a jetty of audit logs records the exact moment of destruction. A farm cannot sell the same deleted data twice, because keeping a hidden copy breaks the attestation.
